clue.text: Seeming attractive, having swapped sides

indicators.note: the sides are left and right, so the L for left is exchanged for R for right

parts.note: something attractive is appealing

explanation.surface: Someone seems charming after changing political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' suggests politics or teams, but it means the letters L (left) and R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe how a thing looks on the surface, as in 'he was seeming calm' and 'appearing calm'.

clue.text: Stage performance as if deaf intermittently

indicators.note: taken at intervals, so the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An actor performs as though only occasionally hard of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera is staged, so it is an example of a stage performance.

clue.text: Part of a garden scheme

definitions.meaning: a small piece of ground for growing vegetables

explanation.surface: A section of garden forms part of a planting plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is both a patch of land and a conspiratorial plan.

clue.text: A jar in the morning for broadcast beginning to appeal

parts.note: AM means in the morning, ante meridiem

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, so the letters entered need only sound like the word

parts.note: the word for is said aloud, and the letters P-H-O-R sound the same when spoken

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone appeals on morning radio for a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is an ancient two-handled jar for wine or oil.

clue.text: Classic ingenuity, boxing Victoria's decoration?

indicators.note: the two words box, or enclose, the letters needed

explanation.surface: Classic cleverness packaging a decoration for Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is not the queen but a Victoria sponge, a British cake, whose decoration might be sugar topping; the question mark signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar frosting decorates a cake such as a Victoria sponge.

clue.text: Punter injured leg in door

indicators.note: an injured thing is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler hurt his leg in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punter' looks like a gambler, but here it is one who propels a boat with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman propels his craft with a pole, much as one punts a boat.

clue.text: Confronted church absorbed by short-lived fashion

indicators.note: being absorbed by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: a fad is a brief craze
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church gets caught up in a passing trend and is challenged over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a problem is to confront it, so the past tense forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Instrument of pressure in armed services

indicators.note: the pressure letter goes in the word for armed services

parts.note: the armed forces are the military services
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A tool used for coercion within the military.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are surgical pincers, a medical instrument.

clue.text: Fellow citizen moving camp to civil disturbance

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A countryman relocates his camp to a scene of unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A compatriot is someone from the same country as you.

clue.text: Depress detectives and try and catch up

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to hear a case is to try it in court

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Detectives depress a suspect by trying and catching up with him.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to make someone lose hope, the same as depressing their spirits.

clue.text: Slump sees daughter, impecunious, coming back

indicators.note: coming back means the word for impecunious is read in the return direction

parts.note: impecunious means poor

explanation.surface: A slump in fortunes leaves a penniless daughter returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: To slump and to droop both mean to sag or sink downward.

clue.text: A person who doesn't know may be stupidly smug on air

indicators.note: done stupidly, the letters are jumbled without sense

explanation.surface: A know-nothing might sound foolishly smug when broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is by dictionary sense someone lacking knowledge, so the descriptive phrase is a plain gloss.

clue.text: Lake in African republic only occupied by a tense business group

indicators.note: the lake's letter sits in the middle of the country's name

parts.note: the Congo is a republic in central Africa
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the word for only is occupied by the following letters, which go inside it

parts.note: mere means only, as in 'a mere child'
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A lake in an African state is taken over by a corporate group.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomerate is a corporation made up of many diverse companies, a kind of business group.

clue.text: Heretic caught invading various locations

indicators.note: the cricket letter invades, entering inside, the jumbled letters
various suggests different arrangements of the letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A heretic is arrested breaking into several places.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs, a heretic against orthodoxy.

clue.text: Owner favouring voting system that's to run

parts.note: pro means in favour of
PR is proportional representation
IE stands for id est, that is
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An owner who backs electoral reform decides to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the owner of a business or property.

clue.text: A pirate's rude song to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting means saying the words aloud for listeners

parts.note: rude means coarse, or vulgar; an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A pirate is about to sing a bawdy shanty on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a privateer or pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Got up wet to get perfume

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
to water something is to wet it

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed soaked and reached for scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose water is a fragrant liquid made from rose petals, used as a scent.

clue.text: Financial institution popular, of course, with Republican

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sure means of course, as an emphatic yes

explanation.surface: A bank, naturally popular, joins up with a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance company is a financial firm that underwrites risk.

clue.text: Soldier's regular letters in verse.

indicators.note: regular letters are every other letter of the word, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A soldier's letters home, written regularly, are in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so it is a piece of verse.

clue.text: Unwrapped smartest things to wear?

indicators.note: with its wrapping removed, the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: snappiest means the smartest or most stylish, as in a snappy dresser

explanation.surface: Unwrapped, these are the smartest clothes to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that babies' nappies are an unglamorous sort of thing to wear; NAPPIES is the British word for diapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappies are garments babies wear, so they are, loosely, items of clothing.

clue.text: Resigns in order to make an entrance

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: Someone quits just so they can make a dramatic entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the formal word for entering or a way in.

clue.text: Give back vacant residence and shop

indicators.note: a vacant word has its interior emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Return an empty house and a shop to their owner.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its owner or former state.

clue.text: Student type of panel supplying energy welcomes central heating

indicators.note: the outer word welcomes the other in, holding it inside

parts.note: a solar panel generates energy from sunlight

explanation.surface: A student's home has solar panels that heat the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: Embarrassing church about call in front of dignitary

indicators.note: the first part is placed before the second
the church abbreviation goes about, or around, the word for call

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is to phone, or call
a worthy is a local notable or dignitary

explanation.surface: A church makes an awkward phone call ahead of a VIP's visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cringeworthy makes you wince with awkwardness or shame.

clue.text: Right — step up and go through again

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An instruction to step forward and repeat a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or review what has been said.

clue.text: Very keen on batting — test opener originally!

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is batting is in

indicators.note: originally points to the beginnings of the two words

explanation.surface: A cricket fan is thrilled the Test opener is batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something, informally, means being enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge study on male chromosome

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
Y is the chromosome carried only by males

explanation.surface: A scientist rejects research on the Y chromosome.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to reject its truth or refuse to admit it.

clue.text: Genuine article pinched by relative in charge

indicators.note: pinched by means held tight inside, as if squeezed

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A genuine item has been stolen by a relative who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinched' suggests theft, but here it means squeezed in, a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic and genuine both mean real, not fake.

clue.text: Spike protecting new weapon

indicators.note: the outer word protects the letter by surrounding it

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: A spike guarding a new weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights.

clue.text: Conditions for parts of school year

definitions.meaning: the British school year is split into three teaching periods

explanation.surface: Rules governing the divisions of an academic year.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms are both contract conditions and the periods into which British schools divide the year.

clue.text: Vacant role for each politician in theatre

indicators.note: a vacant word is emptied of its middle, leaving its ends

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An empty role awaits each politician on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertory is a theatre company performing a rotating set of plays, so the word names such a theatre.
